tldr: No moves from Simplii's direct Canadian competitors except BMO's quantum-computing claim, which is not customer-facing. The news is mostly Brazilian and LatAm Black Friday card offers, plus signals on AI-agent checkout, 23/5 trading and wallet reach.
themes: Black Friday card and cashback promos
AI in payments and markets (agentic checkout, quantum, AI-stock access)
Fintechs becoming banks and shifting fees

highlights.headline: Klarna is now available when an AI agent checks out for a shopper through Adyen Agentic.
highlights.why: Agent-initiated payments are moving into production. Simplii should check whether its cards and wallets, and its fraud and authorization rules, can handle purchases made by an agent rather than a person.

highlights.headline: Nasdaq has published a 23/5 Trading Information Hub, a sign that near-round-the-clock trading is being prepared.
highlights.why: If US markets move toward 23/5, Simplii's self-directed investing clients will expect extended-hours access. That affects order handling, funding cut-offs and support hours.

highlights.headline: Google Wallet has launched on iOS across the US.
highlights.why: Wallet apps are broadening their reach beyond a single phone platform. Simplii should review its own wallet provisioning and the experience for iOS users.

highlights.headline: BMO says it has reached 'quantum utility', with quantum techniques helping AI models pick out the most relevant information in complex datasets.
highlights.why: This is the only item from a direct Canadian competitor. It is an R&D claim with no customer-facing product yet, but it shows how BMO is positioning on AI and data capability.
